'''Montpellier Hérault Sport Club''' ({{IPA|fr|mɔ̃pəlje eʁo spɔʁ klœb|lang}}; {{langx|oc|Montpelhièr Erau Sport Club}}), commonly referred to as '''Montpellier HSC''', is a French professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Montpellier]], [[Occitania (administrative region)|Occitanie]], [[France]]. The club's origins date back to 1919, but it was officially founded in 1974 through a merger of both ''Stade Olympique Montpelliérain'' and ''AS Paillade''.<ref>{{cite web |title=50 years of Montpellier HSC! |url=https://ligue1.com/en/articles/l1_article_1282-50-years-of-montpellier-hsc |publisher=Ligue 1 |access-date=6 August 2025}}</ref>

The club currently competes in [[Ligue 2]], the second level of [[Football in France|French football]]. They play their home matches at the [[Stade de la Mosson]], located within the city. The first team is managed by [[Zoumana Camara]].

Montpellier is owned by Laurent Nicollin, the son of Louis Nicollin, a French entrepreneur, who had been owner since 1974. The club have produced several famous players in its history, most notably [[Laurent Blanc]], who has served as manager of the [[France national football team|France national team]]. Blanc is also the club's all-time leading goalscorer. [[Eric Cantona]], [[Roger Milla]], [[Carlos Valderrama]] and [[Olivier Giroud]] are other players who have played in Montpellier's colours. In 2001, Montpellier introduced a [[Montpellier HSC (Ladies)|women's team]]."}}
